The Houston Rockets are learning how thin their margin for error is when they miss core rotation pieces, as they navigate a tough stretch with both Steven Adams and Clint Capela sidelined by injury. As the roster deals with this frontline crunch, head coach Ime Udoka has had to get creative, leaning heavily on small-ball combinations out of necessity.
 Without Adams and Capela to anchor the middle, the structural weight of the frontcourt falls mostly on Alperen Sengun. Sengun is forced to shoulder heavy minutes as the team's primary traditional big man, battling larger frontlines and expending immense energy on both ends just to keep Houston competitive on the glass.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The lack of standard center depth means Sengun has to carefully manage foul trouble, knowing there is very little room for error behind him, making his role even more difficult.
 To survive these minutes without traditional size, Udoka has had to rely on hyper-active small-ball lineups that lean on versatility and hustle. This is where players like Tari Eason become absolute lifesavers for the rotation. Eason's relentless motor, knack for crashing the glass, and multi-positional defense allow the Rockets to punch above their weight class even when they are drastically undersized.
 Eason has seen extended minutes out of position at center. Although he has been providing sold interior defense and securing vital rebounds, he is much better on the wing as a forward.
 Once Adams and Capela return to the floor, Udoka will gain the luxury of staggering his center rotation to maintain 48 minutes of non-stop physical interior play. On top of that, Udoka announced that neither Adams nor Capela will play both games of back to backs, and the two will stagger their days on the court.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Both centers are expected to return by the end of this month. Their return should prove beneficial for both Sengun and Eason. Rather than overloading Sengun with taxing defensive reps, Udoka can cycle through matchup-specific looks based on opposing frontcourts.
 Inserting Adams alongside non-Sengun lineups preserves high-level offensive rebounding and brutal screen-setting without forcing Sengun to play out of position. Meanwhile, Capela provides a classic rim-running, vertical spacer who can anchor the paint when the defense needs to turn up its transition protection.
 Staggering these veteran bigs will also dramatically relieve the defensive burden on guys like Tari Eason. Instead of grinding out minutes against opposing centers, Eason can shift back into his ideal role as a free-roaming disruptor on the perimeter and wing.
 With Capela and Adams eating up space in the paint, Sengun can preserve his energy to operate as Houston's offensive hub, giving the Rockets a versatile choice of how to operate the frontline, allowing the team to adapt to almost any situation
